There are a series of ministerial meetings and agreements between European countries called the European Union. This includes The Swedish higher education system. It has a participant condition of signing the agreement that all 50 signatory states that participate in European Heritage Days have signed.

This chunk is about:
- Systems: Swedish higher education system, European Higher Education Area (EHEA)
- Organizations: Council of Europe, European Commission
- Concepts: Bologna Process, European Cultural Convention
- Events: European Heritage Days

Facts:
- On 19 December 1954, the Council of Europe opened the European Cultural Convention for signature in Paris as an international treaty.
- The Swedish higher education system is part of the Bologna Process.
- The Bologna Process consists of ministerial meetings and agreements between European countries to ensure comparable standards and quality in higher-education qualifications.
- Signing the European Cultural Convention is one of the conditions for becoming a participating state in the Bologna Process and the European Higher Education Area.
- European Heritage Days is a joint action of the Council of Europe and the European Commission that involves all 50 signatory states of the European Cultural Convention under the motto "Europe: a common heritage".
